subject: Renewal: Support Accelerator — latency sprint & credit allocation
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Porter <ellie@finovate.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Renewal: Support Accelerator — latency sprint & credit allocation

Hi Ellie,

Hope you're well — as we approach the Dec 1 renewal for Finovate, I wanted to propose a concise path to upgrade your support posture without stretching the procurement process. Key asks from our last call were: clearer latency SLOs across gen/embeddings, a short credit to smooth migration costs, and a streamlined onramp for ops/oncall.

Overview proposal (high level):
- Support Accelerator (addendum): premium response tier + 24/7 incident paging for critical routes
- Latency sprint SLOs: 95th pctl targets (text gen: 120–160ms depending on payload; embeddings: 40–70ms) with a fall-back model variant for degraded capacity
- Credit allocation: one-time renewal credit of $60k to be applied across the first 2 monthly invoices (split option available)
- Onboarding: 2-week ops ramp, shared runbook, dedicated onboarding pairing session

I've attached a term sheet that lays this out in a single page to make procurement easier (Support_Accelerator_TermSheet.pdf). If this direction looks good, we can:
1) lock terms and produce an addendum for signature,
2) schedule the onboarding sprint window (target week of Dec 8),
3) confirm credit split (single PO vs split credit).

Do you want me to loop in procurement directly or would you prefer to share the term sheet first? Happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to run through numbers.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin | Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Support_Accelerator_TermSheet.pdf

From: Ellie Porter <ellie@finovate.com>

Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 10:31:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Renewal: Support Accelerator — latency sprint & credit allocation

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clean summary. A couple of clarifying items before I pull procurement in: 

- The credit: can it be applied against the dedicated capacity invoice or only hosted usage? We run a mix of both.
- The latency SLOs: are those measured at the API gateway (us) or at the model instance (Redwood)? We need clear measurement points for our internal SLIs.
- Embeddings: critical for our recommender; we need a tighter percentile for embeddings — is 40–70ms a 95th or 99th number?

I've attached our standard security questionnaire that procurement will expect (Finovate_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). If you can confirm the two bullets above I can loop procurement and our legal ops for a single PO addendum.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Renewal: Support Accelerator — latency sprint & credit allocation

Ellie — thanks for the quick review and for sharing the security questionnaire. Answering inline: 

- Credit application: Flexible. We can apply the one-time $60k credit to either hosted consumption or to the first two invoices for Dedicated capacity, or split (up to 70/30). If you prefer a single PO for the addendum, we can invoice the credit as a negative line item on the first renewal invoice.

- Measurement point for latency SLOs: Redwood reports SLOs from our edge measurement (the request at the configured regional endpoint) with optional customer-side telemetry ingested for comparison. For contractual SLOs we recommend our edge measurement as the source of truth; we can include a reconciliation clause that allows Finovate to bring customer-side telemetry for dispute resolution.

- Embeddings percentile: our suggested target of 40–70ms was intended to be 95th. For mission-critical recommender traffic we can offer a tighter 95th pctl (<=45ms) on a subset of routes if you agree to route pinning (pin those route ids to a reserved pool).

Operational next steps I propose: 
1) I will update the term sheet to include measurement definitions + the split credit options.
2) Draft addendum and a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) for signature.
3) If procurement wants a single PO, Marcus — can you confirm whether Woodside (billing) can accept a negative credit line on invoice? If not, we'll do credit allocation across two invoices.

I've attached a starter MAP template (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) and will push an updated term sheet by EOD Monday. If that timeline is tight, we can expedite.

If you can send the redlined addendum + the DocuSign link, we'll route to legal and procurement this week. Target: sign-off by Nov 27 so onboarding can start first week of Dec.
